scope: free finite-q LLL ordered stress/current kernel and constrained polar metric, distinguished from induced response

primary_sources.title: Polar-metric/axial-gauge perturbations of the Maldacena-Milekhin-Popov wormhole
primary_sources.read_scope: Sections 5.2, 5.4, 5.5 and 6.1-6.4 read; earlier section 9 and state review retained. No full-paper review claimed.
findings: The angle-parametric expectation lift assumes l much smaller than sqrt(q).
Free chiral radiation changes constrained metric components but not its polar master fields at the stated perturbative order.
Induced anomaly pressure and Hall current cannot be discarded when geometry is varied.
Section 6.4 qualifies the proposed action representative and Euler coefficient; no first-principles 4D determinant derivation is claimed.
primary_sources.limitations: Asymptotically flat MMP perturbation and its mean response are not the large-C RN-AdS interacting quantum state; it is not used as a physical noise bound.

ordinary_derivation: Finite-q stress vertex follows by direct fixed-projector Dirac reduction.
Mixed stress is the axial derivative of the projected current; it is not identically zero.
Ordered spectra follow from actual filled-sea fermion particle-hole transitions.
Traceless polar source reconstructs h_ab=2 kappa^2 t_ab/[l(l+1)] with zero polar masters.
Time-smearing and angular orthogonality give a complete convergent polar metric variance sum.

verification_history.changes_after_initial: Renamed fractional metric component output to avoid calling it a lapse; included the note hash. No numerical formula or tolerance changed.

novelty: Known free-field and finite-flux methods; no claim that the vanishing direct master source is new.
